title: Apple explains why HomeView couldn’t launch until now
snippet: Apple’s new HomeView was reportedly mostly finished for years, but kept getting delayed. Here’s why HomeView couldn’t launch until now, per quotes from key Apple execs. more…
fullText:
Apple’s new HomeView was reportedly mostly finished for years, but kept getting delayed. Here’s why HomeView couldn’t launch until now, per quotes from key Apple execs.

Apple touts Siri AI with personal context and conversational abilities as essential to HomeView

In November 2024, Mark Gurman published an in-depth report on the product we now know as HomeView. At the time, he said Apple was targeting a March 2025 launch. But that date kept slipping, and now HomeView will finally arrive in homes on November 13, 2026.

Why the long wait? Gurman has repeatedly pointed to Siri AI as the chief cause of delays. And Apple execs have now largely confirmed that in quotes given to The Verge.

Jennifer Pattison Tuohy asked Kaiann Drance, Apple’s VP of product marketing for home, why now was the right time for HomeView and Apple’s renewed smart home push.

She said Siri AI and the personal context it brings, which she called Apple’s “privacy story,” came together with a device designed specifically for the home. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” she said.

HomeView is being marketed as a shared device that taps into users’ personal context in a way that wasn’t possible pre-Siri AI. So it’s easy to see how Apple’s main pitch would need to change without the more personalized Siri.

A similar explanation was given by Apple’s Lilian Rincon, VP of product marketing for AI. She told The Verge that Siri AI is core to HomeView because it’s “much more capable” and also highlighted its conversational abilities, which make it easy to use for any family member.

“It’s great because you can just ask it to change the temperature on your thermostat in a very natural way. As the Siri AI capabilities continue to evolve, the home experience is fitting to be able to interact with in this natural way.” On why now, Rincon says the natural-language shift is the point where AI goes mainstream. “Because now it can be … my mother-in-law or the Gen Z who’s in college, both of them can use this in the way that they naturally speak and get what they want.”

	

This emphasis and explanation also makes HomeView’s absence in the EU more understandable. 

If Siri AI was simply a nice-to-have addition to an otherwise feature-rich product, perhaps it could launch in the EU still. But if the whole value proposition revolves around the new assistant and its personalized features, waiting until Siri AI is available for iOS in the EU makes more sense.

You can read The Verge’s full article here for more quotes and context.

title: Galaxy S27 might drop to 8GB of RAM; other Android phones could go back to 4GB
snippet: As the AI industry continues to directly cause a crisis in the availability of RAM, new rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 could downgrade to 8GB of RAM, while other Android brands could go back to 4GB for some models. more…
fullText:
As the AI industry continues to directly cause a crisis in the availability of RAM, new rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 could downgrade to 8GB of RAM, while other Android brands could go back to 4GB for some models.

RAM allotments in modern smartphones are fairly predictable. 12GB or 16GB in a high-end flagship, at least 8GB in most mid-range devices, and around 6GB in most entry-level devices. 4GB isn’t uncommon in entry-level devices, but even the most affordable models have pushed to 6GB in recent years because, frankly, Android just doesn’t run all that well on 4GB anymore. 

But everyone is feeling the strain of the rapidly rising cost of memory. A recent report even claims that Samsung doesn’t make a profit when it sells a Galaxy device.

With that in mind, it’s not entirely surprising to hear that Samsung is considering a downgrade for its upcoming Galaxy S27 series. Leaker and analyst @kro_roe on Twitter/X says that the Galaxy S27 series will see its base models start with 8GB of RAM rather than the 12GB that’s been standard for the past two generations. Specifically, Galaxy S25 and Galaxy S26 both start with 12GB of RAM, with a 16GB option for select trims of the Ultra model.

	

This latest leak shows configurations with 8GB of RAM as the starting amount, and 12GB across the Pro and Ultra tiers.

Galaxy S27: 8GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB

Galaxy S27+: 8GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB

Galaxy S27 Pro: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB “under consideration”

Galaxy S27 Ultra: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB/1TB

	

The same leaker says the price increases “may be unavoidable” and that promos like doubled storage may not show up during the pre-order period. Meanwhile, the actual storage type could also differ, with some models “differentiating UFS storage versions” to balance costs. Galaxy S26 used UFS 4.0 across the board.

Samsung might not be alone in these downgrades. Another leaker on Weibo claims that “several” other Android brands are dropping their “top-of-the-line” devices to 12GB, their “main” mid-range models to 8GB, and entry-level devices to 6GB as the “top-of-the-line” offering, with most of those lower-cost Android phones going back to just 4GB of RAM.

It’s hard to know for certain what the future holds at this point, as “RAMageddon” rages on. All we know is that everything is getting more expensive. Thanks AI.

title: Apple says developers are showing ‘incredible’ support for the iPhone Duo
snippet: One of the major issues raised by early reviews of the iPhone Duo is limited support by third-party apps. As we noted in our own review, there are three tiers of support currently, the worst of which sees an iPhone app stranded in the center of a mostly black area of the display. The good news is that Apple says the position is changing rapidly, citing “incredible” support for the larger display of the folding iPhone … more…
fullText:
One of the major issues raised by early reviews of the iPhone Duo is limited support by third-party apps. As we noted in our own review, there are three tiers of support currently, the worst of which sees an iPhone app stranded in the center of a mostly black area of the display. 

The good news is that Apple says the position is changing rapidly, citing “incredible” support for the larger display of the folding iPhone …

Apple says developers are taking advantage of the flexibility of the iPhone Duo in order to create exciting new experiences.

With an inner display that’s 50 percent larger than iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the flexibility to use iPhone Duo in a variety of poses, developers are enhancing their apps to create exciting new experiences for capturing and sharing memories, streaming entertainment, gaming, multitasking, and much more […]

“The response to iPhone Duo from our developer community has been incredible, and we’re inspired by how quickly they’ve embraced its larger display and new ways to interact,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations. “From watching popular shows and content on the expansive inner display to multitasking across windows or playing console-quality games, developers around the world are reimagining what their apps can do. We can’t wait for users to discover these experiences beginning this Friday, with many more app experiences to follow.”

The company says it will be highlighting some of the best iPhone Duo apps and games on the App Store tomorrow when the new device goes on sale. Apple has already named some of them, starting with streaming video services.

 Netflix makes finding great entertainment even more fun: Members can scroll through Clips on the outer display and then open iPhone Duo to keep watching on the large nano-texture inner display, with Clips switching seamlessly between a vertical or horizontal view.

More streaming services — including Prime Video and Paramount+ — are joining Apple TV in using the larger canvas for movies and series. With iPhone Duo, Prime Video enhances the viewing experience for users as they stream premium entertainment, and when partially folded, content plays on the top half of the display while X-Ray details showing cast and bonus content appear on the bottom half. Paramount+ offers richer playback controls and expanded browsing for shows and live channels.

Two key sports apps have also been updated to take advantage of the new opportunities.

When iPhone Duo is propped open on a table, users can easily enjoy content hands-free, without a stand. Sports fans can follow MLBand PGA Tour with live games and highlights, plus real-time scores, stats, and leaderboards on the larger display.

“Baseball fans are incredibly passionate about the sport, and they follow our games as closely as they can. Now, iPhone Duo provides an exciting new fan engagement platform by showcasing the action and information simultaneously,” said Kenny Gersh, MLB’s executive vice president of Media, Business Development, and Product. “This incredible device unlocks a fun, versatile way to experience baseball from anywhere, and we’re grateful to have worked with Apple to ensure the app is ready for the World Series. Set iPhone Duo on a table partially folded and the live game plays on the upright half of the display while real-time stats fill the half resting on the table, so fans never have to choose between the broadcast and the box score.”

Apple says that Microsoft Word and Outlook will roll out a desktop-class experience in the next few weeks, while Zoom, Slack, and Salesforce are also prepping their own updates.

Zoom turns the inner display into an immersive video conference room, so users can see shared content and other participants at the same time. Slack brings a user’s whole workspace into view, making it easy to follow channels and automate tasks. Salesforce helps teams manage customer relationships and act on business insights, with more of their dashboards in view.

The company goes on to name other apps, including Fantastical, Notewise, Things, Bear, Detail, Instagram, Edits, and VLLO. Apple Arcade games ready for the new form factor include Sneaky Sasquatch and Retrocade.

More apps and sample screenshots are shared in the company’s announcement.

If you’ve already ordered the iPhone Duo or are heading to an Apple store to try one, reviewers recommend trying the inner display in both landscape and portrait modes to see which delivers the better experience. Different third-party apps tend to be optimized for one or the other.

title: Wyze Solar Cam has a 2K camera and needs just an hour of sunlight to keep recording
snippet: Wyze is launching a new Solar Cam that has a camera that matches the best Google Nest has to offer, while needing just an hour of sunlight to avoid needing to manually recharge. more…
fullText:
Wyze is launching a new Solar Cam that has a camera that matches the best Google Nest has to offer, while needing just an hour of sunlight to avoid needing to manually recharge.

Wyze has a camera for basically every need, and its latest is one that works outdoors with potentially limitless battery life. The Wyze Solar Cam bundles a 2K camera with a 1.77W solar panel that Wyze says needs just an hour of direct sunlight to keep charged.

The camera houses a 5,200 mAh battery to ensure it can run in the case of crummy weather or having its solar panel blocked, but in direct sunlight, the panel doesn’t need much to maintain the battery. That’s nothing super new – Wyze itself launched a Solar Cam Pan with the same promise last year, and plenty of other brands have done the same. You can even add a solar panel to a Nest Cam if you really want to.

The benefit of this latest Wyze Solar Cam comes partially in the resolution, with a 2304 x 1296 2K camera that features 130-degree field of view and color night vision. It also has a 100 lumen spotlight built-in and optional local microSD card recording. 

	

Wyze Solar Cam is available today for $69.98, with the camera also available without the solar panel for $10 less.

fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m reading about an incredible medical plagiarism scandal, replaying the original Ocarina of Time ahead of its remake’s November 5th release, jamming to the dark new Fontaines D.C. album, and using Gemini to prep for the upcoming fantasy basketball season.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

Over the course of Friday, it quickly became clear that demand for the iPhone Duo far outstripped initial supply. Apple’s first foldable went on sale at 8am on the 16th, and delivery dates immediately got pushed back to November, then December, and now January. Analysts had warned that Apple wouldn’t be able to keep pace with interest, despite the phone’s $2,000 price, but the company called it “nothing short of extraordinary” in a statement released to the media.

	

Samsung was benefiting before Apple even opened the order books. Its UK mobile leadership says purchases of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 family are up 16% since launch, while Google searches for Samsung foldables rose 300% over the preceding month.

The big question, though, is whether the Duo’s existence will bring the book-style foldable — and by extension, the $2,000 smartphone — into the mainstream. Samsung has been beating this drum since 2019, but foldable share still sits at a mere 2% of the overall smartphone market, and most units sold are the smaller, cheaper flip-style variety. The Duo is expected to give Apple a 25% share of the entire foldable market by the end of 2026, which should broaden acceptance of the form factor across the industry.

I’m not surprised by the uptick in interest; the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is undoubtedly my favorite foldable ever, owing to its novel and pocketable design. I’ve always enjoyed reading on book-style foldables, but with the Fold 8 I often forget I’m using a phone entirely.

Will there be a day when, say,  a decade from now, foldables are the conventional smartphone choice and slab phones of any kind are considered budget alternatives? In a world where component prices stay elevated and companies continue to pad their margins with premium options at the expense of the entry class, that’s a real possibility. Either way, the Duo validates far more than Samsung’s decision to experiment with foldables all those years ago; its unprecedented demand hints at a sea change in how people want to use their phones, and the compromises they’re willing to accept in order to get there.

iPhone Duo orders are delayed into 2027; here are the Android foldables you should try instead

iPhone Duo has a bigger battery than Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold

✉️ Inbox

The biggest reason not to buy a Googlebook is all about timing. Ben’s Weekender essay focuses on how the Googlebook OS fiasco is exacerbated by the fact that every Googlebook laptop is like $300 too expensive.

HP Googlebook 14 review: Great laptop, shame about the OS. 😬

Google’s Universal Cart puts a shopping cart everywhere, including Search homepage, Chrome

Amazon launches two Bee AI recorders to remember everything you say. Nope. Absolutely not.

Google restricts every free AI Pro trial from Pixel & more compared to paid subscribers

Android 17 QPR2 Beta 7.1 rolling out for Pixel

Spotify’s ‘QR code verification’ cracks down on sharing and could ban you for a year. Yikes, that’s not particularly customer-first, is it?

It’s been a busy week for Samsung news

Samsung just released Android 17 updates for Galaxy S23 and several more devices. Android 17 is a bigger update than one might think, primarily for its improvements to stability and performance.

Samsung’s Android 18-based One UI 10 update sounds like it might be a big deal. One UI 9 is still steaming from the oven, but we’re already dreaming of ways its successor will copy iOS.

I’ve struggled to use Samsung displays for years, but the Galaxy S27 may finally fix that; here’s why

Galaxy S26 Ultra is one of the ‘best inventions of 2026’ thanks to its Privacy Display. Eh.

Galaxy S27 reportedly skips Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 due to overheating. I don’t think this rumor has legs; Samsung always goes with the best SoC available unless it’s an absolute disaster (see the Snapdragon 810 debacle), and I doubt this one is.

Qualcomm says rumors about Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating are ‘inaccurate’

Samsung reportedly hasn’t finalized Galaxy S27 details, considers February launch. Wouldn’t surprise me if they’re trying to keep costs down.

Dizzying lineup of Galaxy Z Fold 9 devices leaks, including the Galaxy Z ‘Slide’. Next year’s Galaxy foldable lineup looks crowded.

🤝 Cc: Ben Schoon

Welcome to Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with Ben Schoon, 9to5Google’s Senior Editor and one of the best disc golf players I know.

Who are you?

Ben Schoon

What do you do for work?

I am the Senior Editor at 9to5Google, covering daily news, reviews, and more.

What do you do for fun?

Disc golf has basically taken over my non-work life. I’ve got a 170-plus-week streak of playing at least once a week, I frequently play in and even run tournaments, and I’m absolutely hooked.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

I still deeply enjoy tech, but the AI era has certainly changed my outlook, and not always in the best ways. On the bright side, it’s cool to see the explosion of what tech can do. On the downside, let’s just say that humanity tends to take the path of least resistance, and AI enables that in some frightening ways.

What are three apps you can’t live without and why?

Nourish has been a huge part of my weight-loss journey over the past couple of years, helping me log food more easily while also connecting with an actual nutritionist. 

UDisc might as well be in my dock row given how frequently I’m out on the disc golf course.

Beeper continues to be indispensable given my multi-device lifestyle.

What is a gadget that you love right now?

The Fitbit Air has been a refreshing bit of simplicity in a busy tech life.

How does AI fit into your life right now?

As mentioned, my relationship with AI isn’t always positive. Lately I find myself more and more frustrated by the impact it’s made on day-to-day life for everyone, and wishing we could go back. Ultimately, I barely find myself using AI in my own life, but I do appreciate those occasional bits of delight that come from finding a good use for it.

What’s a TV show you recently watched and loved?

Recently started listening to the “How We Made Your Mother” podcast and it’s unlocked a fresh rewatch of the early seasons of HIMYM with some new perspectives.

What’s a movie you recently watched and loved?

Project Hail Mary hasn’t left my mind all year. It continues to be a source of joy from its excellent visuals and plot, and the vocal stims that still find their way into daily conversation with my wife and me.

What’s a game you recently played and loved?

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has me hooked right now. I love a good racing game, and this one delivers a real challenge.

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

Spend time around my crazy doggos.

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Over the weekend, I caught up on some podcasts and just happened to listen to an episode of The New York Times’ The Daily from a few days ago. “When A.I. Comes for Your Purpose in Life” features an interview with mathematician and Cornell University professor Steven Strogatz, and is among the most poignant and honest conversations I’ve heard about how AI stands to reconfigure everyone’s jobs — even the ones we previously considered unassailable.

There’s recently been an abundance of great reporting on how AI is changing the fields of mathematics and science. But I think some of it lacks the emotional intelligence to acknowledge that LLMs are not just disrupting jobs and preempting discovery; their seemingly infinite potential undermines what it means to be a human solving problems for their own sake. As people become increasingly comfortable offloading their cognition to machines, what happens to their relationship with their own brains?

🗑️ Trash

Anthropic recently announced that it would set aside 5% of its shares to be used for the “public good,” a vacuous claim that has shades of effective altruism. Elon Musk, who is practically single-handedly bankrolling the Republicans’ midterm election, then came out with a similar, more direct offer: “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.”

The moves are a direct result of a growing public backlash against AI’s negative impacts on culture, on employment, and increasingly on the environment, but laundering one’s reputation with the promise of future beneficence often has the inverse effect.

title: Supernatural Restart: The VR Fitness App Is Back as VR Itself Starts to Change
snippet: Exclusive: Supernatural is relaunching in early access and could expand beyond Meta Quest headsets. Meanwhile, Meta VR Glasses could shape what comes next for fitness.
fullText:
I was heartbroken earlier this year when Supernatural, my favorite VR fitness app on Meta Quest, shut down. But now it’s making a comeback as an indie company. The new app returns this week in early access, with all the same trainers and a focus on getting the classic experience going again. But the funny thing is, just as it’s returning, the very nature of VR is starting to change.

Meta’s VR Glasses, coming next spring, promise to shrink down the future of Meta’s headsets to glasses-like form. And Supernatural’s team feels confident that slimmer, lighter hardware will be an excellent fit for fitness. If so, it could be the beginning of something new. More glasses-like devices on the horizon, including Meta VR Glasses, Google’s Xreal Aura and even Snap Specs, could enable virtual fitness experiences — and everything else VR has promised — in more portable forms that trap less sweat.

But in the meantime, I’m glad the app’s back for Quest. “We’re coming back because people raised their voices and started petitions and said we need this to be part of our lives. We wouldn’t be doing this if that hadn’t happened,” Leanne Pedante, Supernatural’s head of fitness and one of its in-game coaches, said to me of the new, smaller Supernatural team.

			

More from CNET

I talked to Pedante and James Senior, Supernatural Health’s CEO, about the new service and what else could be coming once Meta VR Glasses roll around next year.

Supernatural’s new VR app will initially support controllers, with hand tracking coming later.Supernatural Health

What’s back with Supernatural, and what’s changed

The early-access version of the new Supernatural app — which will once again launch on Quest headsets — will gradually bring back the trainers and music tracks from the Meta-owned version. There will be thousands of workouts, and new 3D environments as well. 

But the concept behind Supernatural, a rhythm-based set of song-driven choreographed game-like workouts with actual human coaches that talk alongside you, remains the same. 

“That coaching you hear is coming out of a person who is physically experiencing the same thing that you are in the moment,” said Pedante, who feels that’s a key ingredient versus opting for an AI companion. “That creates this kind of invisible empathy — the coach is able to anticipate what you need to hear or what your body is probably doing.”

Those 3D landscapes were always one of the most compelling parts of Supernatural, but so were the trainers, who appear in 3D video before workouts and speak in your ears as you punch and swing to each song. I developed an emotional connection to my workout progress.

The songs are being relicensed, according to Senior, but many familiar tracks are coming back, along with new ones. New workouts and content will follow soon after.

“The music deals have really accelerated in the last three weeks,” he said. “We’re pretty much going to have the full catalog back that people have in the old service, and in the coming weeks, we’ll also be bringing back tracks that had disappeared from the Meta service over the last 12-18 months because of licensing restrictions.” 

The original workouts have also been remastered for the new app, with better-synchronized beat mapping across existing Quest headsets. “Each has different components, which very subtly causes clock drift once it reaches the application layer in the platform. In the new app, we’ve built in new logic to account for that,” Senior added.

Senior also told me there’s a special comeback workout in which some of the trainers share their emotional journeys through leaving Meta and going independent, with songs chosen to fit their moods.

But the price is going up to $200 a year, or $20 a month. Original “founding member” Supernatural users will get a $20 discount on the annual plan. 

It looks like a lot of the previous features will be part of the package, too: Fitness history and achievements will come over, and although the new experience has a new companion phone app, it’ll still work for tracking heart rate during workouts. That’s another key part of what made Supernatural actually feel like a real fitness tool for me. But that app and the heart rate tracking aren’t available now. They’re coming later this year.

Meta’s VR Glasses, due next year, are much lighter than a Quest VR headset.Scott Stein/CNET

Meta glasses: The sign of the next wave

One big change down the road will be support for hand tracking. For now, the new Supernatural app still uses controllers to track hand movements during workouts. There’s a good reason for the shift: Meta’s VR Glasses, coming next year, won’t include controllers in the box. The next wave of VR could make hand tracking the default.

Supernatural’s team feels confident that hand tracking is now good enough to step in as a replacement — but also that Meta VR Glasses will be a way for Supernatural and other fitness apps to take a leap forward.

Meta’s upcoming $1,299 VR Glasses have a completely different design from Quest headsets: a glasses-like form with a tethered, phone-sized processing puck.

In a promo image for the new Supernatural, Pedante even poses with Meta VR Glasses. It’s a nod to where the Supernatural team thinks VR fitness is heading. Pedante and Senior see Meta VR Glasses as a perfect fit for where things are going for immersive fitness.

“It’s a lightweight device that’s highly breathable. It’s not susceptible to fogging. It has high definition and, frankly, it’s a device that’s perfect for the fitness use case,” says Senior, who previously worked at Meta on VR platforms.

It’s a bold claim. Until now, there hasn’t been a smaller-scale VR device that’s workout-capable. When I wore Meta’s VR Glasses last month, I wondered how well they’d be able to run apps such as Supernatural. Meta has already confirmed that fit accessories are coming for its VR glasses that could also make them easier to wear during activities such as workouts.

Google’s Xreal Aura, coming this year, is small and can run VR apps. Could it be a fit for fitness apps, too?Scott Stein/CNET

Where else could Supernatural end up?

Supernatural’s team is now independent and no longer tied exclusively to Meta. That opens the door to other platforms, although the VR landscape isn’t as big as it once was. SteamVR could be a possibility. So could Android XR. And perhaps even platforms that aren’t VR at all.

Senior confirmed that for now, Supernatural is still just a Meta app, but other devices are being looked at. I wonder about glasses-like hardware, such as Google’s imminent Xreal Aura or even Snap Specs. An app for Steam VR would be a big step, too.

“It’s this interesting, convergent zone of AR and VR,” Senior said of the Aura glasses, which feel a bit like VR and use different display technology from Meta’s VR Glasses, but a similar processing puck. “That’s an area we would want to experiment and lean in,” he said without committing to whether it might emerge there, too.

Clearly, Supernatural is aiming to be a killer app for Meta’s VR Glasses, and Senior said some of the headset’s features — higher-res displays and eye tracking — might also be incorporated into the experience.

I’m just excited to dive back in. As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine. But I’ll be putting the headset on again, and I’ll let you know what it feels like when I do.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Scott Stein
						

						

							Editor at Large						
					

											

								

											I started with CNET reviewing laptops in 2009. Now I explore wearable tech, VR/AR, tablets, gaming and future/emerging trends in our changing world. Other obsessions include magic, immersive theater, puzzles, board games, cooking, improv and the New York Jets. My background includes an MFA in theater which I apply to thinking about immersive experiences of the future.

title: Supernatural, the best VR workout app, makes its glorious comeback today
snippet: Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today. more…
fullText:
Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today.

Workout trends often come and go like the wind, but a few staples hang around long enough to be properly cemented into the “this really works” category. Supernatural is one such example. The VR workout app debuted on April 23, 2020, making it the best way to get a gym-like workout in a world where all the gyms were shut down during the pandemic. Lots of people used it and continued to use it until earlier this year, when Meta closed the studio that made it.

People were devastated. The entire Supernatural community on Facebook was up in arms. But it wasn’t long until Supernatural’s founders announced that they had acquired the rights and would be returning later in 2026 as an independent company, and today is that day.

Meta Quest 3 at Amazon

AMVR FC4M magnetic face pad (you’ll thank me later) at Amazon

Supernatural Early Access is officially launching today, October 21, on Meta’s storefront. You can get a free 7-day trial by downloading the app, and then it’s $20 per month after that. An extended 14-day free trial is available to folks who sign up for the $200/year plan, which grants a $40 annual discount by paying up front.

	

If you haven’t used Supernatural before, you’re about to be very pleasantly surprised. The game features daily coach-led workouts with popular music you’ll love to work out to. Gamers move their bodies around to the beat, smashing flying obstacles with bats, ducking, kicking, and generally getting very sweaty. The whole thing takes place in incredibly realistic environments, which the Supernatural team says are getting a big visual upgrade in the new release.

Today’s early access version launches with thousands of workouts available immediately — with all the coaches you know and love — including hundreds of licensed music tracks, a brand new home environment set in Laguna Torre, a glacial lake in Argentine Patagonia, and the ability to transfer your entire workout history from the old Supernatural app to the new one. I know my colleague, Daniel Bader, will be very happy about that.

Founding members will start with a custom bat, and more rewards are dropping throughout the early access period. Additionally, household accounts can be used to share the experience with up to four people in your home, including individual profiles for each one. Make sure you get a good face pad that’s easy to clean if you do this!

As Supernatural continues to get rebuilt and gets better than ever, users can expect more workouts and music on a weekly cadence, the return of real-time workouts with friends (sign up for the beta now), a new mobile companion app (that pairs with your smartwatch), new destinations, and plenty of rewards for returning and founding members. It’s incredible, and it’s quite frankly mind-blowing to see the entire team return this way, all without the help of Meta.

title: Here’s where Apple says iPhone Duo will (and won’t) be available for walk-ins
snippet: Are you planning to line up at the Apple Store for a walk-in iPhone Duo purchase? Here’s what Apple says about availability to expect for the new model. more…
fullText:
Are you planning to line up at the Apple Store for a walk-in iPhone Duo purchase? Here’s what Apple says about availability to expect for the new model.

Here is Apple’s official statement on iPhone Duo walk-in availability at Apple Stores

Last week when iPhone Duo pre-orders launched and almost instantly got backordered, many made plans to visit the Apple Store on October 23 in the hope of securing a walk-in purchase.

Today in a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple outlined what to expect from in-store stock around the world.

Here is Apple’s official statement:

“On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves. Here’s where only online orders for pick-up will be available, rather than walk-ins: China Mainland, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and UAE.

If you can’t get an iPhone Duo on launch day, the good news is that reports keep coming in of iPhone Duo pre-order dates being moved up.

title: Google Maps on CarPlay rolling out Gemini when navigating
snippet: Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience. more…
fullText:
Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience.

When using navigation, tapping the Gemini icon on the right edge lets you ask multi-step questions and issue commands like:

“What park is famous for gorgeous views overlooking the city?”

“I want to go at a time when it’s not too busy and the weather will stay nice. Is now a good time?”

“Start navigating me there but make sure to avoid toll roads.”

This is the first time Google Maps is offering voice assistant functionality in CarPlay. Previously, Google Assistant was only available when using Google Maps navigation directly on your iPhone.

Gemini can also be used to report traffic disruptions with your voice. This matches the navigation experience introduced on Google Maps for Android and iOS last year, while it’s already available in Android Auto.

	

Gemini in Google Maps on Apple CarPlay is available now in the US, while the global rollout is underway.

title: Google gives Pixel 9 another year of free Satellite SOS connectivity
snippet: Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out. more…
fullText:
Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out.

Satellite SOS was introduced on the Pixel 9 series and has been in place on every Pixel phone released in the time since. The feature grants your phone access to limited satellite connectivity in emergencies, offering a lifeline in dangerous, off-grid situations. 

But Google only promised this would be free for “the first 2 years after activation.”

A support page footnote still reads:

	

Service included at no additional charge for the first 2 years after activation of devices. Available in select countries and languages. Connection and response times vary based on location, site conditions, and other factors.

Everything you should know about Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 before you ever have to use it

As of August 2026, that timer was up for Pixel 9 series devices. Yet, Google showed no signs of charging for the feature, but it wasn’t exactly clear what would happen next. Now, the company has confirmed that, at least for another year, Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 remains free.

The company confirmed the news to PCMag, saying:

Confirming that we’ve extended this offering, at no additional cost, for one additional year. We have no details to share beyond that at this time.

So far, there have been no hints even behind the scenes of Google introducing a way to charge for Satellite SOS on Pixel phones. Apple, which introduced this functionality prior to Google, recently confirmed that it would also be extending the “free trial” of satellite connections for iPhone 14, 15, and 16, and there’s also no word on what Apple might charge for the feature.

Would you pay for Satellite SOS on your Pixel if Google starts charging for it?

title: TikTok accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos
snippet: TikTok has been accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos posted on its platform. The allegations were made by former and current employees, who say that the company failed to properly respond to internal reports … more…
fullText:
TikTok has been accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos posted on its platform. The allegations were made by former and current employees, who say that the company failed to properly respond to internal reports …

NPR reports.

Employees raised the alarm about minors appearing in sexual content on the app, which viewers could pay to access and the company would profit from – a potential financial crime. They also flagged that users under 18 were using loopholes to bypass age-restricted content and to block parents and guardians from reviewing their activity on the app. TikTok also refrained from conducting surveys to assess the ages of its users because it was concerned that it would have to turn the results over to the Federal Trade Commission, the documents show.

Employees say that senior leaders were aware of the issues, but their responses were inadequate. Social media companies are required by law to report suspected CSAM, as well as suspicions regarding money being obtained illegally through their platforms.

The report additionally says concerns were expressed internally about young users being shown content related to suicide and self-harm, and that the platform was not taking proper steps to tackle this.

TikTok is one of the most popular apps on the App Store, with a high proportion of teenage users. The company responded by saying that the claims made in the story are “clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works.”

title: MagSafe Monday: Upgrading to the iPhone Duo? This MagSafe battery was built specifically for it
snippet: With the iPhone Duo bringing an entirely different shape to the iPhone lineup, you’ll need accessories built for it as well. BMX built the SolidSafe Duo specifically around the iPhone Duo. It’s designed to fit perfectly on the back without bleeding over and includes a stand. more…
fullText:
With the iPhone Duo bringing an entirely different shape to the iPhone lineup, you’ll need accessories built for it as well. BMX built the SolidSafe Duo specifically around the iPhone Duo. It’s designed to fit perfectly on the back without bleeding over and includes a stand.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

The reason the SolidSafe Duo fits the iPhone Duo’s proportions is the battery cell itself. In this MagSafe battery, BMX used a custom-made 5,000mAh semi-solid-state cell rather than a standard lithium-ion cell, which gave them the flexibility to build a compact form factor built for the iPhone Duo’s specific dimensions. A standard battery cell wouldn’t have allowed that without the battery overhanging the edges or sacrificing too much on the capacity.

The semi-solid-state battery contains significantly less liquid electrolyte than conventional lithium-ion batteries. With less liquid, there is less flammable material inside the cell, which reduces the fire risk associated with heat, physical damage, or internal short circuits. We’ve all seen enough battery recalls to understand why this is important.

The 360-degree stand

The integrated rotating ring stand is designed around how people will use the iPhone Duo. Portrait mode is for reading and iMessage, and landscape for video, partially folded for hands-free calls. The stand rotates 360 degrees and stays attached as the phone’s position changes, so you don’t have to remove the battery pack every time you shift how you’re holding the iPhone Duo.

Charging speeds and the built-in cable

The SolidSafe Duo battery charges your iPhone Duo at up to 15 watts per MagSafe or up to 20 watts through the attached USB-C lanyard cable. The cable stays with the power bank, which means no separate charging cable to pack or lose track of. It also handles input of up to 15 watts via that same cable to recharge it.

A full-color LCD on the battery displays remaining battery capacity and live charging wattage simultaneously, so you can see both how much power you have left and how fast it’s actually charging.

Wrap up on the SolidSafe Duo battery

The SolidSafe Duo is priced at a premium over generic/budget MagSafe battery packs, but with the iPhone Duo, you’ll want to have accessories designed specifically for it to maximize its value, so it’s worth a look. It’s likely that less expensive batteries will be launched in the coming months, but if you want one at launch, this looks like a solid option.

You can pick up the new SolidSafe Duo from Amazon or directly from BMX.

snippet: Google is delivering an update to Android’s earthquake alerts system that will show more information while also expanding support to over 200 regions across the globe. more…
fullText:
Google is delivering an update to Android’s earthquake alerts system that will show more information while also expanding support to over 200 regions across the globe.

Launched in 2021, Android’s earthquake alerts system uses the sensors in Android smartphones to detect the earliest signs of an earthquake and provide a precious few seconds of warning prior to destructive impacts. While the system has had a couple of mishaps, it has also saved lives and Google says it has sent over a billion alerts. 

Effective today, the Android earthquake alerts system is now live in more than 200 regions across the globe, up from 98 previously. Google specifically calls out Panama and Guatemala as new additions. 

Beyond the regional expansion, Google is also updating the design of earthquake alerts. Specifically, the “Be Ready” step is going to offer more information on the location of the earthquake’s epicenter and the estimated magnitude.

	

Google says:

Be Aware: A straightforward alert for estimated light shaking, letting you know an earthquake has been detected nearby.

Be Ready: A detailed alert for stronger shaking, alerting you to prepare to take action.

Take Action: A full-screen alert for moderate to heavy shaking, giving you immediate advice on how to stay safe.

We’ve built-out our Be Ready alert with new helpful guidance. In the coming months, you’ll see a map with a radius of where we’ve detected shaking, estimated earthquake magnitude, action you can take, and a button to learn more about the earthquake as information comes in.

title: Samsung reportedly hasn’t finalized Galaxy S27 details, considers February launch
snippet: It would be “February at the latest,” but Samsung has yet to set a launch date under pressure to finalize component details for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra. more…
fullText:
It would be “February at the latest,” but Samsung has yet to set a launch date under pressure to finalize component details for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra.

Samsung’s launch schedule has been laid on the same path for years, with minor deviations here and there. The newest Galaxy S device gets released in January or February every year, right after CES and before MWC comes around.

According to a leak by Lanzuk on Naver, Samsung has set the Galaxy S27 series launch date on the fence. The laker says that, at the latest, Samsung would be looking at a February launch, so it’s not an expansive gap between releases that we might be looking at. If Samsung settles on January, even better.

The possible push may be due to Samsung reportedly not having finalized the full component list for the Galaxy S27 series. More specifically, the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra. The base and Plus models are essentially finished, if this leak is reliable.

	

The post credits RAMageddon for the timing adjustment. It notes “there are differing opinions regarding the composition and ratio” of the devices. Read straightforwardly, it implies Samsung hasn’t decided how much memory to inject into the two most expensive devices in this lineup.

A potential storage standard upgrade to UFS 5.0 seems to be the biggest contributor to the Galaxy S27’s undecided launch timing. LPDDR6 is also a costly addition, and incorporating UFS 5.0 on these models means they need the hardware to perform, given they both sit at a price point that seems to fluctuate from high to higher.

There’s no concrete timing, and even Samsung has yet to set the date. Still, it looks like it’s highly unlikely Samsung will make any last-minute changes as big as swapping phone models, like last year.

title: Google Chrome Will Notify You If You’re on a Scam Website
snippet: You’ll need to opt into Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode to use the new features.
fullText:
Google’s Chrome will start showing alerts for suspicious or dangerous websites when Enhanced Protection mode is on.

Google’s Chrome browser is adding several new features to help guide people away from websites known for scamming visitors, including sites that try to trick people into opening their computers to vulnerabilities.

In a Tuesday blog post, Google outlined a series of new features that can kick in as long as Enhanced Protection mode is enabled.

If the browser detects you’re on a suspicious website, Chrome displays a clear, “This site doesn’t seem right” pop-up warning. That warning will show as an overlay over the content, with the option to instead mark the site as safe. But that’s just if the site is suspicious. For websites that Google deems as dangerous, meaning that they’re commonly associated with causing harm, a full red page showing the warning will appear. It will direct the user away from continuing.

			

More from CNET

The new feature focuses on helping users avoid fake antivirus and browser update scams, even creating a scam likelihood score.

Chrome will also fight against ClickFix scams, in which a website tricks someone into copying and pasting code into their computer, often under the pretense of fixing a fake vulnerability. When Chrome detects that someone is being tricked into copying code on such a site, it will clear the clipboard and display a warning message. This is meant to help stop the practice in real time since, if successful, it could allow a scammer to gain full access to one’s device.

To use these features, users must opt into Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode via the browser’s privacy and security settings.

The security suite provides real-time defenses—such as blocking “ClickFix” social-engineering attacks—in exchange for sharing additional browsing data with Google. Users should weigh this enhanced protection against the expanded data collection before enabling the feature.

snippet: You probably shoudn’t buy a Googlebook. fullText:
You probably shoudn’t buy a Googlebook. That’s less of an opinion about the platform itself, but more about the bad timing that this launch has seen, and protecting your own wallet.

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every Sunday along with ‘Inbox’ on Tuesday and Thursday. You can find past issues here.

Googlebook as a platform isn’t magically a competitor to Windows and macOS. Rather, it inhabits nearly the exact same space in the market that Chromebook did. The app gap hasn’t been fixed, nor has Google managed to build a platform that someone can go without the deep ecosystems that the dominant players have built out for decades.

If a Chromebook wasn’t for you, Googlebook isn’t either

Googlebook OS review: A post-smartphone PC, if Google can keep it

There are any number of reasons I could give you not to buy a Googlebook right now. The price tags. The lack of apps. The simple fact that this is a brand new platform you shouldn’t fork over hundreds of dollars to beta test. But, ultimately, I think the biggest reason you shouldn’t be buying a Googlebook is timing.

	

RAMageddon is in full swing, thanks in no small part to Google and its AI competitors, and consumers are paying the price for it. Everything has gotten extraordinarily expensive, and it’s not slowing down anytime soon. Price hikes will continue, and you’re only going to feel the strain more and more. 

With that in mind, why would anyone spend their money on a Googlebook?

That’s really what I’ve been wrestling with the past few weeks in the midst of Google’s big push. Googlebook is asking you to spent $1,000, give or take, on a laptop that’s not fully capable because… it works with your phone? Truly, I just cannot fathom making that choice when you could pay the same, if not less, for a Windows laptop or a MacBook.

From my HP Googlebook 14 review earlier this week:

Especially at a time when the cost of laptops continues to skyrocket, I cannot recommend that anyone invests $1,200 into a Googlebook when you can get a Windows laptop, or even a MacBook, for the same price, if not less. There’s simply no reason to get less functionality for the same price…

Imagine a scenario. You spend $1,000 or more on a Googlebook today because, right now, it fits your needs. You could have bought a MacBook Air for just a little more, or a Lenovo laptop for a little less. But you reason that, for now, the Googlebook does everything you need it to do. But, six months from now, you pick up a new hobby, change jobs, or have any number of things change that impact what you need from your tech. Suddenly, that Googlebook might not cut it. The problems Googlebook has today are not going to be solved in six months; many, if not all, of the limitations you face today will still exist.

That’s my reasoning for why I won’t buy a Googlebook. What do you think?

title: Anthropic takes on ChatGPT Dots and Meta Muse with Claude Duet
snippet: Anthropic is introducing a new AI assistant that can proactively manage tasks across connected apps, keep track of emails and calendars, and continue working even when the app is closed. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Anthropic is introducing a new AI assistant that can proactively manage tasks across connected apps, keep track of emails and calendars, and continue working even when the app is closed. Here are the details.

’A proactive agent that understands what needs your attention’

Anthropic today announced Claude Duet, an always-on AI agent currently rolling out as a research preview to Pro and Max subscribers in the US, with access gradually rolling out via a waitlist.

The feature is included at no additional cost, but counts toward existing plan usage limits, including work performed in the background, which the company notes could cause users to reach those limits “sooner than with chat alone.”

Here’s Anthropic on its new proactive AI assistant:

Claude Duet is a research preview of Claude that you message the way you’d message a person. Tell it what you need, typed or spoken, and it works in the apps you’ve connected, lets you know when something needs you, and is designed to ask before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything.

The company says invitations will go out in waves and adds that “Claude Duet isn’t available on Team or Enterprise plans yet,” though it plans to expand availability to those subscriptions in the future.

We’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.

It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. pic.twitter.com/kt8gAbWuX8

— Claude (@claudeai) October 21, 2026

Anthropic says that Claude Duet uses the same memories, skills, and connectors as regular Claude, and can even search past conversations so users don’t have to repeat themselves.

Claude Duet runs on its own cloud-based computer, allowing it to continue working even after users close the app.

Additionally, Claude Duet offers integrations with Stripe to check for unpaid invoices and draft payment reminders, as well as Link and Shop Pay to make purchases with user approval.

Here are a few use cases described by Anthropic:

Message it like a person. Type a message or record a voice message. Your main thread stays in one place, so Claude Duet picks up where you left off. You can also start separate channels for different topics, and they share the same memory.

Start the day with a brief. Each morning, it looks across your email and calendar, picks what most needs your attention, and can start the first steps, like drafting replies for you to review. Through the day, it sends updates on the work it’s doing and follows up on threads that have gone quiet.

Hand it larger jobs. Describe what you need, and it works out which apps to use and how much effort the job takes. Bigger results come back as files you can review and edit, such as a research brief, a financial model, a slide deck, or a dashboard. Finished work appears in the Make tab.

Add plugins. Claude Duet supports plugins, such as the small business plugin, and can suggest ones that fit your work.

Use websites without a connector. For sites that don’t have a connector, Claude Duet uses its own browser in the cloud.

According to Claude Duet’s support page, the assistant also has a dedicated Tasks tab where users can track ongoing work and see which tasks need their attention.

Claude Duet also sends updates to the main conversation when a task is completed or requires a decision. Importantly, only users can mark tasks as finished.

Anthropic says Claude Duet is powered by Claude Opus 5.5 and is available through standalone apps for iOS and Android, as well as on the web at claude.ai, for users who receive an invitation.

title: Insta360 launches a cheaper version of its wireless mics with color screens
snippet: Following the launch of its wireless Mic Pro system last May featuring built-in color E Ink screens for custom branding and an array of three microphones to emulate different pickup patterns, Insta360 has announced a cheaper alternative that skips a few features many content creators might not miss. fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Following the launch of its wireless Mic Pro system last May featuring built-in color E Ink screens for custom branding and an array of three microphones to emulate different pickup patterns, Insta360 has announced a cheaper alternative that skips a few features many content creators might not miss.

The new Insta360 Mic sits between the company’s Mic Pro and the budget-friendly Mic Air, which uses much smaller screenless transmitters. While the Mic Pro is priced at $329.99 for a kit that includes two microphone transmitters, one wireless receiver, and a charging case, the Insta360 Mic costs $249.99 for a similar bundle. Insta360 sells the microphones individually since they can directly connect to smartphones and many of the company’s cameras (including the X6, X5, and Luna Ultra) over Bluetooth. The Mic Pro transmitter on its own costs $99.99, while the new Insta360 Mic is $79.99.

The design and functionality of the Insta360 Mic is very similar to the Mic Pro. It has the same 1.22-inch, six-color E Ink display on the front that can be customized with logos, photos, or solid colors to help it blend into clothing. The transmitters have a range of up to 400 meters when paired with Insta360’s wireless receiver that can connect to professional cameras, laptops, or other recording devices using a built-in USB-C connector. The Insta360 Mic also features AI-powered noise canceling to reduce background noise and automatic gain control modes that adjust recording levels on the fly to help prevent clipping if things suddenly get too loud.

So what are you missing out on when choosing the cheaper Insta360 Mic? The biggest downgrade is that the transmitters have just a single mic instead of the triple mic array in the Mic Pro, so you cannot select from multiple pickup patterns; omnidirectional is the only option. However, that simplified hardware makes the transmitters slightly lighter than the Mic Pro’s — 19.4 grams compared with 19.7 grams — and battery life increases from up to 10 hours to up to 13 hours, which can be boosted to 34 hours with the charging case.

The Mic Pro’s transmitters come with 32GB of built-in storage for creating a backup recording. The Insta360 Mic transmitters don’t have any built-in storage, but you can enable backup recording by sticking a microSD card inside each one. As with the lighter design and improved battery life, the microSD option also feels like an upgrade for the Insta360 Mic if you want more than 32GB of storage.

fullText:
Snap Specs are available for pre-order now, and actor Robert Downey Jr. is joining the team after he said he “was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds.”

That makes Robert Downey Jr. the latest big-name partnership from Snap, as the company gets ready to launch its first true consumer-ready smart glasses, simply called Specs. Downey Jr. join the team at Snap as the honorary Chief Customer Experience Officer (CCEO), putting him in charge of showing the world just how close to his Iron Man roots these glasses really are.

Snap is clearly challenging Meta’s market leadership in the XR category with a product that combines elements of Meta Ray-Ban Display Glasses and the upcoming Meta VR Glasses. Specs are a completely standalone pair of smart glasses with displays in each lens, plus full hand-tracking support that’s typically only found on a bulkier VR headset.

	

Snap has been building up to the Specs release since 2016 (not a typo). The company has released several experimental developer-only smart glasses during that time, all of which were significantly bulkier than Specs now looks, with huge improvements between each generation.

In addition to the clear Iron Man nod, Snap has also partnered with HBO to launch a Specs Harry Potter experience to coincide with the new HBO show, plus an official partnership with the NBA. title: The ESA’s Euclid Telescope Discovered a New Comet Completely by Accident
snippet: It was identified in Euclid telescope imagery using software designed to detect moving objects.
fullText:
Approximately 40 to 70 new comets are discovered every year, most of which are found by astronomers actively looking for comets or at least new celestial bodies in general. But at least one comet discovered in 2026 doesn’t have that distinction. It was discovered entirely by accident by a telescope that was not actively looking for comets. 

Say hello to C/2026 S1 (Euclid), a brand new comet that was just discovered by the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope. The comet is located about 1.3 billion kilometers away from Earth, which is roughly the distance between the sun and the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn. It was discovered by Mikko Pöntinen of the University of Helsinki, together with the Solar System Objects Science Working Group, who were using the Euclid telescope at the time of discovery. 

What makes this one weird, among the thousands of other comets humans have named, is how they found it. The group was intentionally pointing the telescope away from the elliptical plane, a band in the sky where the solar system’s planets, most of its asteroids and a significant number of its comets reside. The idea was to avoid the cosmic dust and debris left behind by those celestial bodies, allowing the group to take clearer pictures of distant galaxies in deep space. 

			

More from CNET

While doing this, a comet zipped through. It could have gone entirely unnoticed, but Pöntinen had written software to identify moving objects, which flagged images where the comet appeared. Pöntinen was then able to use its speed and trajectory to find it in other images and report it as a new comet. 

“I was excited to see my software flag a ‘streak’ smeared across several images,” Pöntinen said in a statement. “Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas.”

A happy coincidence

Euclid appears in imagery as a fuzzy little streak that could have gone entirely unnoticed by humans.ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, M. Pöntinen et al. 2026

The most interesting part of C/2026 S1 (Euclid) is undoubtedly that it was discovered by a telescope that wasn’t designed to find comets on a mission that also wasn’t designed to find comets. 

According to Bruno Altieri, archive scientist and member of the Euclid solar system team, this is because of the way the Euclid telescope works. It spends most of its time in a wide survey that will eventually map about one-third of the extragalactic sky, which encompasses all the planets, radiation clouds, debris clouds and other structures outside of the Milky Way galaxy. 

It also employs a “step-and-stare” method of mapping the cosmos, which means it “steps” to a spot, stares at the sky for about an hour and then moves on. That means much of what it looks at is only looked at once. Since comets are often found thanks to their movement, it’s hard to identify such an object with this observation method.

Euclid also conducts a deep field survey. These are zoomed-in glimpses of specific parts of space conducted periodically around the schedule of the wide survey. These parts are revisited only a handful of times per year, and that’s the only reason C/2026 S1 (Euclid) was discovered. 

“This discovery is indeed a happy coincidence as few comets are expected to be discovered by Euclid,” Altieri said. 

Straight up from the sun

The comet is at the “top” of its orbit currently and it’s estimated to be thousands of years before it can circle back. European Space Agency

Very little is known about C/2026 S1 (Euclid) so far, as it’s only been imaged a few times. There are a few things that astronomers have already gleaned from what they have seen. For starters, this is a long-period comet, which means its orbit around the sun lasts more than 200 years. The exact time hasn’t been calculated, but early estimates put it at thousands of years before it completes a full orbit.

According to Altieri, that means it almost certainly came from the Oort Cloud, which is a shell of icy bodies, rocky planetesimals and other debris that surrounds the entire solar system. Comets from the Oort Cloud are referred to as “nearly isotropic” comets and orbit the sun from all sorts of zany angles. C/2026 S1 (Euclid) is no different. 

Space doesn’t have an up or down, but if it did, C/2026 S1 (Euclid) would be straight up from the sun as viewed from Earth. Its sweeping orbit takes it far above the solar system before cutting between Saturn and Jupiter on its way back down. It’s expected to reach perihelion — the point where it’s closest to the sun — in 2027. After that, it won’t be back there for thousands of years.

title: Tesla says it will start selling Cybercabs by end of year
snippet: Tesla said Wednesday it will start selling its Cybercab to customers by the end of the year, even as federal regulators investigate whether the vehicle meets vehicle safety standards. The gold-hued, autonomous two-seater lacks a steering wheel and other traditional controls. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Lars Moravy, vice president of engineering at Tesla, […]
fullText:
Tesla said Wednesday it will start selling its Cybercab to customers by the end of the year, even as federal regulators investigate whether the vehicle meets vehicle safety standards. The gold-hued, autonomous two-seater lacks a steering wheel and other traditional controls. 

During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Lars Moravy, vice president of engineering at Tesla, said the Cybercabs produced today are all destined for the company’s own robotaxi fleet. As that fleet grows, the company will “mainly deliver fully designed autonomous vehicles to our customers,” he said, noting that it will start small. The company will scale as it learns about delivery, ownership, and fleet management of autonomous vehicles, Moravy added. 

Tesla first floated the idea of selling the autonomous vehicle to third parties last month around its Cybercab event in Austin and even posted a form for people interested in buying robotaxis. But it wasn’t clear if Tesla would follow through, or how.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has talked for years about building a massive fleet of low-cost robotaxis, but until recently, those plans centered on turning privately owned Tesla vehicles into self-driving taxis with a software update.

That plan has yet to materialize, and Musk’s comments on the call show how his views have shifted.

Today, Tesla owners can subscribe to Full Self-Driving (Supervised), an advanced driver-assistance system that automates many driving tasks but still requires the driver to take control. The company continues to push out software updates to the system to improve its capabilities, but a human driver is still required to remain engaged and ready to take over — even though many videos show drivers testing the limits of that rule.

Musk said Wednesday that an unsupervised version of FSD, the fully self-driving version, would be rolled out to customers sometime in the second quarter of next year, yet another delay for Tesla owners, many of whom bought or subscribed to the software years ago.

If both timelines hold, it would mean third-party fleet customers would be able to buy the autonomous Cybercab and potentially operate it as a robotaxi service before Tesla owners would get access to the same autonomous capability in their own cars.

Musk said the Cybercab is meant to be a ride-hailing vehicle, not a car people own. “Cybercab is primarily going to be something that is offered as like transport as a service, whereas our other cars would be more, you know, the cars that you’d want to own, like the 3 and the Y and whatnot, and the Roadster, obviously,” Musk said Wednesday on the call. “But, you know, the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and transported as a service.”

There is at least one obstacle that could throw off Tesla’s Cybercab fleet plans. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the federal auto safety regulator, announced last month that it had opened an investigation into the Cybercab, just hours after the vehicles began operating on public streets in Austin.

Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) require manual controls like brake pedals, as well as other features such as rearview and side mirrors. Automakers traditionally self-certify whether their vehicles comply with FMVSS rules, and Tesla did the same.

Current regulations don’t accommodate vehicles without manual controls, though the Department of Transportation recently proposed removing those requirements for vehicles that are designed to be autonomously driven. In the meantime, NHTSA said it would investigate the Cybercab to “examine the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.”

The outcome of that investigation could affect whether Tesla, or anyone else, can legally operate the Cybercab.

		Kirsten Korosec is a reporter and editor who has covered the future of transportation from EVs and autonomous vehicles to urban air mobility and in-car tech for more than a decade. She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.

title: Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook could debut on November 6: Here’s what to expect
snippet: After over a decade of not adopting touch displays on its Mac notebook lineup, Apple will finally be releasing its first touchscreen MacBook as early as November 6th, after announcing it as early as October 27th. more…
fullText:
After over a decade of not adopting touch displays on its Mac notebook lineup, Apple will finally be releasing its first touchscreen MacBook as early as November 6th, after announcing it as early as October 27th.

Of course, rumors are rumors – though essentially every reputable source has aligned on the idea of the MacBook Pro gaining support for touch very shortly. Apple even left a few hints in macOS 27: Touch Support in Sidecar, pull to refresh support, and slightly bigger menu bar items.

One could call all of this a mere coincidence, but it’s probably exactly what it looks like. Regardless, here’s what the first touchscreen MacBook will have to offer.

OLED, Dynamic Island

On the display panel side of things, the redesigned MacBook Pro will come with a Tandem OLED display. This will be similar to the iPad Pro, which is often touted as one of the best mobile displays on the market. Tandem OLED comprises of stacked OLED panels, which allows for incredible colors, strong contrast, and increased brightness.

Reports also suggest it’ll come with a Dynamic Island, and it’ll be a bit smaller than the one on the iPhone. It won’t, however, come with support for Face ID.

Software optimizations

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple will have some special optimizations for the first touchscreen MacBook Pro, beyond what’s already visible in the betas of macOS 27:

“For instance, if users touch a button or control, the interface will bring up a new type of menu surrounding their finger that provides more relevant options for touch commands.

The software will also display the most appropriate set of controls based on users’ prior interaction. And if a person taps an item in the menu bar at the top of the screen, the set of controls will enlarge to be more easily selectable with a finger.”

M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

Despite initial reporting suggesting that we’ll be seeing the debut of the M6 Pro and Max in the redesigned MacBook Pro, Apple is now skipping the release of those chips to accelerate the M7. This means that the first iteration of 2nm chips won’t be making their way to the redesigned MacBook Pros, and they’ll instead offer the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

There won’t be a base model version of this computer quite yet, though rumors suggest that Apple will be launching a base version of the redesigned MacBook Pro with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly thinner chassis, significantly lighter

One design rumor for the new MacBook Pro is the fact that it’ll be slightly slimmer and lighter – though it’s unclear how meaningful this will be. The last MacBook Pro iteration made the computers look and feel quite chunky, so a bit of progress here would likely be welcome – so long as it doesn’t come at the compromise of thermals.

Bloomberg has also reported that these computers will be ‘significantly lighter,’ thanks to re-engineering of internal components.

Release date

title: Walmart’s $60 Google TV streamer might be the only good deal left in streaming
snippet: As prices skyrocket on virtually everything else, Walmart’s $60 Onn 4K Pro streamer with Google TV might be the only good deal left — if you can find it in stock. more…
fullText:
As prices skyrocket on virtually everything else, Walmart’s $60 Onn 4K Pro streamer with Google TV might be the only good deal left — if you can find it in stock.

Prices on streaming hardware have exploded in recent months. Just a few examples include:

Google TV Streamer: Was $99, now $149

Apple TV 4K: Was $129, now $299 (new model)

Nvidia Shield TV Pro: Was $199, now $299

Roku Ultra: Was $100, now $150

It’s rough out there folks. AI is totally worth it, right?

Anyway, all of those price hikes have had me revisiting the Walmart Onn 4K Pro that launched earlier this year and that I’ve been using in one of the rooms in my house for the past few months. Put simply, it gets the job done very well, and is a tremendous deal compared to everything around it.

	

The most direct comparison to the Onn 4K Pro is the Google TV Streamer, and they are pretty close across the board. They have virtually identical software, though Google’s first-party release obviously gets updates and new features a bit quicker. Performance is also nearly identical, with the only big difference being 4GB of RAM in Google’s streamer vs 3GB in Walmart’s. Most of the time, it doesn’t matter.

Walmart’s streamer continues to be a good performer day-in and day-out, and there are little things I actually prefer over Google’s. Topping that list would be the remote, which is a bit more comfortable and backlit, the latter being invaluable in a dark room at night. I could do without the slightly obnoxious “Free TV” button, but I’m overall quite happy with the remote, and even more so with the find remote button on top of the actual streaming box.

					

Google TV on a speedy set-top box with solid hardware and a good remote, all for $60. It’s the best deal in streaming, enough said!

					

				

Pros

				

											

Enough horsepower for speedy Google TV performance

											

Comfortable, backlit remote

											

Plenty of ports

									

			

					

				

Cons

				

											

Hard to find in stock

											

Fabric is hard to clean if it gets dirty

									

			

			

The hardware itself is unassuming with a fabric top and a footprint similar to any other streaming box. That fabric top won’t be a problem for most but, crazy tip, don’t spill anything on it! It’s basically impossible to clean if it gets dirty.

As far as ports go, you’ve got HDMI, Ethernet, full-size USB-A, and the whole thing draws power from USB-C instead of a barrel plug like the last generation — dreams do come true!

	

All of that comes together for just $60. It’s nothing ground-breaking, sure, but this is just a good streamer in every meaningful way without costing an arm and a leg like virtually everything else does right now. The biggest headache is just finding the thing in stock. We’ve been tracking stock for months and, finally, Walmart seems to be more consistently selling Onn 4K Pro both in stores and online, but your results may still vary depending on when you go to buy and where you live. 

Onn 4K Pro at Walmart

If you can’t find the Pro, Walmart also has its Onn 4K Plus dongle that costs just $50 and, in most ways, matches up with the Pro. The main things you’re giving up are the Ethernet port, USB-A port, and a bit of performance.

title: The Atari VCS saga will come to an end next year when its software store closes
snippet: Following a decade long saga of delays, name changes, and Atari having to assure backers of a crowdfunding campaign that its retro console wasn't doomed, the Atari VCS platform is being retired early next year. On February 1st, 2027, the Atari VCS software store is shutting down, according to an announcement posted to the Atari Club Discord and shared by Tom's Hardware. With a design loosely inspired by the original Atari 2600 - minus a cartridge slot - the VCS was a Linux-based, AMD-powered mini PC that could emulate a large collection of pre-loaded classic Atari games, but its functionality could be expanded through an online software sto … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Following a decade long saga of delays, name changes, and Atari having to assure backers of a crowdfunding campaign that its retro console wasn’t doomed, the Atari VCS platform is being retired early next year. On February 1st, 2027, the Atari VCS software store is shutting down, according to an announcement posted to the Atari Club Discord and shared by Tom’s Hardware.

With a design loosely inspired by the original Atari 2600 — minus a cartridge slot — the VCS was a Linux-based, AMD-powered mini PC that could emulate a large collection of pre-loaded classic Atari games, but its functionality could be expanded through an online software store that included access to streaming platforms, and in recent years, game streaming platforms like Xbox Cloud Gaming and Nvidia GeForce Now.

Atari VCS owners will still be able to download and add software to their libraries through Atari’s official online store up until January 31st, 2027. After that the store will officially shut down, but previously downloaded apps and games will still be usable. Atari says that following the store’s closure it plans to “make an OS update available that allows you to migrate all functionality to your local machine, removing any dependencies on Atari infrastructure for authentication and software.” The company also plans to release an Atari Home Brew app allowing owners to continue to add new games to their console’s library shared to the community by third-party developers who still want to develop and support the VCS.
